results.name: complex_false_object_rate
results.description: On word trials, the proportion of choices falling on false objects possessing high visual complexity (at least 2 features, the highest feature count among non-matching objects in the display).
results.code:
# name: complex_false_object_rate
# description: On word trials, the proportion of choices falling on false objects possessing high visual complexity (at least 2 features, the highest feature count among non-matching objects in the display).
def test_statistic(df):
    sub = df[df["query"] == "utterance"]
    lookup = {}
    for _, row in sub[["objects", "utterance"]].drop_duplicates().iterrows():
        objs = json.loads(row["objects"])
        utt = int(row["utterance"])
        false_indices = [i for i, o in enumerate(objs) if o[utt] == 0]
        if false_indices:
            false_fcs = [sum(objs[i]) for i in false_indices]
            max_f = max(false_fcs)
            if max_f >= 2:
                lookup[(row["objects"], row["utterance"])] = [1 if (objs[i][utt] == 0 and sum(objs[i]) == max_f) else 0 for i in range(len(objs))]
    obj_strs = sub["objects"].to_numpy()
    utts = sub["utterance"].to_numpy()
    choices = sub["choice"].to_numpy(dtype=int)
    picks = [lookup[(s, u)][c] for s, u, c in zip(obj_strs, utts, choices) if (s, u) in lookup]
    return float(np.mean(picks)) if len(picks) > 0 else 0.0

def test_statistic(df):

    lookup = {}

        fcs = [sum(o) for o in objs]

            lookup[s] = [1 if fc == n_feats else 0 for fc in fcs]
    choices = sub["choice"].to_numpy(dtype=int)
    picks = [lookup[s][c] for s, c in zip(sub["objects"], choices) if s in lookup]
    return float(np.mean(picks)) if len(picks) > 0 else 0.0

results.name: word_intermediate_match_rate
results.description: On word trials where matching candidates span at least three distinct feature counts, the proportion of choices falling on strictly intermediate-complexity matching objects.
results.code:
# name: word_intermediate_match_rate
# description: On word trials where matching candidates span at least three distinct feature counts, the proportion of choices falling on strictly intermediate-complexity matching objects.
def test_statistic(df):
    sub = df[df["query"] == "utterance"]
    lookup = {}
    for _, row in sub[["objects", "utterance"]].drop_duplicates().iterrows():
        objs = json.loads(row["objects"])
        utt = int(row["utterance"])
        matching = [i for i, o in enumerate(objs) if o[utt] == 1]
        matching_fcs = [sum(objs[i]) for i in matching]
        if len(matching_fcs) >= 3 and min(matching_fcs) < max(matching_fcs):
            min_m, max_m = min(matching_fcs), max(matching_fcs)
            flags = [1 if (objs[i][utt] == 1 and min_m < sum(objs[i]) < max_m) else 0 for i in range(len(objs))]
            if any(flags):
                lookup[(row["objects"], row["utterance"])] = flags
    obj_strs = sub["objects"].to_numpy()
    utts = sub["utterance"].to_numpy()
    choices = sub["choice"].to_numpy(dtype=int)
    picks = [lookup[(s, u)][c] for s, u, c in zip(obj_strs, utts, choices) if (s, u) in lookup]
    return float(np.mean(picks)) if len(picks) > 0 else 0.0

results.name: non_nested_fewer_features_rate
results.description: On word trials where matching candidates have different feature counts and cross-cutting (non-nested) features, the proportion of choices for the candidate with the fewest total features.
results.code:
# name: non_nested_fewer_features_rate
# description: On word trials where matching candidates have different feature counts and cross-cutting (non-nested) features, the proportion of choices for the candidate with the fewest total features.
def test_statistic(df):
    sub = df[df["query"] == "utterance"]
    lookup = {}
    for _, row in sub[["objects", "utterance"]].drop_duplicates().iterrows():
        objs = json.loads(row["objects"])
        utt = int(row["utterance"])
        matching = [i for i, o in enumerate(objs) if o[utt] == 1]
        fcs = [sum(objs[i]) for i in matching]
        if len(matching) >= 2 and min(fcs) < max(fcs):
            min_i = matching[int(np.argmin(fcs))]
            max_i = matching[int(np.argmax(fcs))]
            o_min, o_max = objs[min_i], objs[max_i]
            if not all(o_min[k] <= o_max[k] for k in range(len(o_min))):
                min_fc = min(fcs)
                lookup[(row["objects"], row["utterance"])] = [1 if (objs[i][utt] == 1 and sum(objs[i]) == min_fc) else 0 for i in range(len(objs))]
    obj_strs = sub["objects"].to_numpy()
    utts = sub["utterance"].to_numpy()
    choices = sub["choice"].to_numpy(dtype=int)
    picks = [lookup[(s, u)][c] for s, u, c in zip(obj_strs, utts, choices) if (s, u) in lookup]
    return float(np.mean(picks)) if len(picks) > 0 else 0.0

def test_statistic(df):

    lookup = {}

results.name: two_object_subset_target_rate
results.description: On 2-object word trials where candidate objects have a strict subset-superset feature relationship, the proportion of choices for the minimal subset object (the pragmatic target).
results.code:
# name: two_object_subset_target_rate
# description: On 2-object word trials where candidate objects have a strict subset-superset feature relationship, the proportion of choices for the minimal subset object (the pragmatic target).
def test_statistic(df):
    sub = df[df["query"] == "utterance"]
    lookup = {}
    for _, row in sub[["objects", "utterance"]].drop_duplicates().iterrows():
        objs = json.loads(row["objects"])
        if len(objs) != 2:
            continue
        utt = int(row["utterance"])
        o0, o1 = objs[0], objs[1]
        if o0[utt] == 1 and o1[utt] == 1:
            is_0 = all(o0[k] <= o1[k] for k in range(len(o0))) and sum(o0) < sum(o1)
            is_1 = all(o1[k] <= o0[k] for k in range(len(o0))) and sum(o1) < sum(o0)
            if is_0 or is_1:
                target = 0 if is_0 else 1
                lookup[(row["objects"], row["utterance"])] = target
    obj_strs = sub["objects"].to_numpy()
    utts = sub["utterance"].to_numpy()
    choices = sub["choice"].to_numpy(dtype=int)
    picks = [1 if c == lookup[(s, u)] else 0 for s, u, c in zip(obj_strs, utts, choices) if (s, u) in lookup]
    return float(np.mean(picks)) if len(picks) > 0 else 0.0

results.name: mumble_singleton_when_duplicates
results.description: On mumble trials in displays containing both unique singleton objects and duplicate objects, the proportion of choices falling on unique singleton objects.
results.code:
# name: mumble_singleton_when_duplicates
# description: On mumble trials in displays containing both unique singleton objects and duplicate objects, the proportion of choices falling on unique singleton objects.
def test_statistic(df):
    sub = df[df["query"] == "prior"]
    lookup = {}
    for s in sub["objects"].unique():
        objs = json.loads(s)
        tuples = [tuple(o) for o in objs]
        counts = [tuples.count(o) for o in tuples]
        if any(c > 1 for c in counts) and any(c == 1 for c in counts):
            lookup[s] = [1 if c == 1 else 0 for c in counts]
    choices = sub["choice"].to_numpy(dtype=int)
    picks = [lookup[s][c] for s, c in zip(sub["objects"], choices) if s in lookup]
    return float(np.mean(picks)) if len(picks) > 0 else 0.0

results.name: ambiguous_word_singleton_rate
results.description: On word trials where the heard utterance is true of all objects in the display and candidates include both a unique singleton and duplicate objects, the proportion of choices for the singleton object.

# name: ambiguous_word_singleton_rate
# description: On word trials where the heard utterance is true of all objects in the display and candidates include both a unique singleton and duplicate objects, the proportion of choices for the singleton object.
def test_statistic(df):
    sub = df[df["query"] == "utterance"]
    lookup = {}
    for _, row in sub[["objects", "utterance"]].drop_duplicates().iterrows():
        objs = json.loads(row["objects"])
        utt = int(row["utterance"])
        if all(o[utt] == 1 for o in objs):
            tuples = [tuple(o) for o in objs]
            counts = [tuples.count(o) for o in tuples]
            if 1 in counts and any(c > 1 for c in counts):
                lookup[(row["objects"], row["utterance"])] = [1 if counts[i] == 1 else 0 for i in range(len(objs))]
    obj_strs = sub["objects"].to_numpy()
    utts = sub["utterance"].to_numpy()
    choices = sub["choice"].to_numpy(dtype=int)
    picks = [lookup[(s, u)][c] for s, u, c in zip(obj_strs, utts, choices) if (s, u) in lookup]
    return float(np.mean(picks)) if len(picks) > 0 else 0.0
